title: Design Patterns: What, Why and When
description: A design pattern is a reusable way of organizing collaborating functions or objects for a recurring design problem; it is a decision template, not copy-paste code.

blocks.title: Simple but deep explanation
blocks.content:
Simple explanation

A design pattern is a reusable way of organizing collaborating functions or objects for a recurring design problem; it is a decision template, not copy-paste code.

Why this pattern or principle matters

Patterns help teams communicate and reduce the cost of repeated change, but a pattern with no real variation only adds indirection.

How I would implement it

Describe the changing requirement, define the smallest stable contract, hide the varying implementation behind it, and verify the boundary with a second implementation or test double.

When to use it

the same kind of change repeats, implementations must be replaceable, or direct dependencies make testing difficult.

When not to use it

there is one simple stable implementation and a direct function is clearer.

title: Coupling, Cohesion and Change
description: Coupling is the dependency between units, while cohesion is how strongly the responsibilities inside one unit belong together.

blocks.title: Simple but deep explanation
blocks.content:
Simple explanation

Coupling is the dependency between units, while cohesion is how strongly the responsibilities inside one unit belong together.

Why this pattern or principle matters

High unnecessary coupling spreads one business change across unrelated components, and low cohesion mixes API, UI, policy and storage concerns.

How I would implement it

Group code around one business purpose, expose a small contract, map external data at the boundary, and examine which files repeatedly change together.

When to use it

changes frequently spread across unrelated files, tests need many real dependencies, or circular imports are growing.

When not to use it

splitting code into tiny units would make one coherent workflow harder to understand.

title: Composition Over Inheritance
description: Composition builds behavior by combining small collaborators, while inheritance reuses behavior through an is-a hierarchy.

blocks.title: Simple but deep explanation
blocks.content:
Simple explanation

Composition builds behavior by combining small collaborators, while inheritance reuses behavior through an is-a hierarchy.

Why this pattern or principle matters

Deep inheritance couples children to parent internals and makes independent combinations of behavior difficult.

How I would implement it

Extract each varying behavior into a function or contract and pass it to an orchestrator; use inheritance only for a stable, behaviorally valid subtype.

When to use it

formatting, validation, exporting, caching or authorization vary independently.

When not to use it

a small genuine subtype hierarchy is stable and substitution is correct.

blocks.content:

ISP means consumers depend only on the capabilities they actually use.

Why this pattern or principle matters
